memory_candidates.content: state-write.sh's --audit-verdict flag reads the whole FILE's parsed JSON into one jq --argjson shell argument. If any single NDJSON line in that file exceeds Linux's per-argv MAX_ARG_STRLEN (131072 bytes) -- easy to hit when audit-task-proposals.sh runs against a backlog with hundreds of file_scope-less entries, since every one emits a scope-blind verdict -- the call fails with exit 126 'Argument list too long'. Workaround: build a condensed verdict file first (keep every non-scope-blind verdict verbatim, collapse the scope-blind entries into a single scope_blind_count integer) and pass that to --audit-verdict instead of the raw audit output; the full raw audit NDJSON can still be committed separately as durable evidence.
